findings.description: GL2IsConjugateSubgroup is documented as a decision procedure ('determines whether K is conjugate to a subgroup of H'), but when K has level 1 (K = gl2N1 = full GL(2,Zhat)) and H is a proper subgroup, the correct answer is false; instead the code asserts GL2Order(H) eq GL2Size(#BaseRing(H)) and crashes with an assertion failure. (The identical assert in GL2ConjugateSubgroup at line 2026 is defensible because conjugacy is a documented precondition there, but IsConjugateSubgroup must return false.)

For N=1 the returned function yields the empty sequence [] instead of the integer index 1. The docstring says the function computes 'the index of the similarity invariant of an element ... in the sorted list of similarity invariants'; GL2SimilaritySet(1) = {@ [] @} has exactly one entry, so the index is 1 (an integer, as for all N>1). The N=1 shortcut `return func<M|[Z|]>` was copy-pasted from GL2SimilarityClassMap (where returning the invariant [] IS correct). The bug propagates to SL2SimilarityClassIndexMap(1), GL2PrimitiveSimilarityClassIndexMap(1) and SL2PrimitiveSimilarityClassIndexMap(1), which all delegate here (all four N=1 similarity sets have exactly one entry, so 1 is the correct index for all of them). Internal callers are unaffected because they short-circuit at N=1, but the public contract is violated.

The docstring states that with Sparse the entries are pairs '[n,i] such that the ith similarity invariant occurs n times in H', but the code (line 2609) returns pairs [i,n] with the INDEX first and the count second. A caller trusting the documented order would silently swap indexes and counts (both are small integers, so no type error would flag it). Also 'elment' is a typo.

The docstring claims that with Sparse 'a second parameter giving the corresponding index of each count is also returned', but the intrinsic returns a single sequence of [i,n] pairs (line 2669), exactly like the GL2 version; there is no second return value.
findings.proposed_fix:
Line 2646 current:
  If Sparse is true, only nonzero counts are returned and a second parameter giving the corresponding index of each count is also returned.
Replacement:
  If Sparse is true, only nonzero counts are returned and each list element is a pair [i,n] such that the ith similarity invariant occurs n times in H.

findings.description: The docstring of SL2SimilarityCounts(N::RngIntElt) says '(i is an index into GL2SimilaritySet(N))' but the counts are indexed by SL2SimilaritySet(N) (the code builds S:=SL2SimilaritySet(N) at line 2516 and returns one count per SL2 similarity invariant). Copy-paste drift from the GL2 version at line 2504.

Two errors in the docstring (repeated at 2476 for SL2PrimitiveSimilaritySet, and the 'prime power order' error also at 2485 GL2PrimitiveSimilarityClasses and 2494 SL2PrimitiveSimilarityClasses): (1) primitive similarity classes correspond to conjugacy classes of ALL cyclic subgroups (divisions in the sense of the GL2PrimitiveSimilarityIndexes docstring), not 'cyclic subgroups ... of prime power order' -- restricting to prime-power order would give a strictly smaller set and would also break the documented Gassmann-equivalence property (a permutation character is not determined by its values on prime-power-order elements); (2) the Set variants return a sorted indexed set of similarity invariants, not a 'Sequence of tuples <inv,rep>' (that description belongs to the Classes variants).

GL2SimilarityReps (2324), SL2SimilarityReps (2334), GL2PrimitiveSimilarityReps (2344) and SL2PrimitiveSimilarityReps (2354) all carry the identical docstring 'Sorted indexed set of similarity invariants in GL/SL(2,Z/NZ)', but they return a sequence of representative MATRICES, one per (primitive) similarity class, ordered to match the corresponding SimilaritySet; the two Primitive variants also fail to mention they are restricted to primitive classes. (Additionally the declared return type SetIndx is actually SeqEnum.)

Docstring says 'Read list of primitive similarity indexes for GL(2,Z/NZ) from disk' but the intrinsic reads the SL2 table (sl2psfile) into ZZ`SL2Cache["psindexes"]. Copy-paste from the GL2 version at line 2374.

findings.description: Dead/confused error handling in the catch block: cnt is assigned via ExactQuotient, which returns an integer or raises, so the subsequent 'if Denominator(cnt) ne 1 then ... error e; end if; cnt := Numerator(cnt);' can never trigger/does nothing; if the retry's ExactQuotient fails, the error propagates uncaught from inside the catch block instead of reaching the intended 'Retry failed' diagnostic. Functionally harmless (the result is correct whenever a value is returned; all four algorithms verified to agree), but the recovery logic does not do what it appears to intend -- compare the cleaner retry in GL2SimilarityCounts (lines 2599-2607). Either the retry should compute m*#Fix(pi(g))/n as a rational (matching the Denominator/Numerator handling) or the Denominator check should be dropped.
findings.evidence: Code inspection (lines 2626-2634): cnt := ExactQuotient(m*#Fix(pi(g)),n) inside catch; ExactQuotient(a,b) in Magma raises 'Arguments have no exact quotient' rather than returning a rational, so Denominator(cnt) is always 1. Behavior of the normal path verified empirically: for Borel(8), NonsplitCartan(9), Borel1(6) and random g, GL2SimilarityCount(H,g:Algorithm:=alg) agrees with brute-force counts for all four algorithms.

findings.description: NOTE: this intrinsic begins at line 662, just past my assigned range (1-661); reporting because it is confirmed broken. In the Schreier-orbit loop the transversal entry for a newly discovered point z := y^g is set to T[z] := a*g where a := T[y]*g was already computed, so T[z] = T[y]*g*g maps the base vector to z^g, not z (compare the correct 'T[z] := a;' at line 652 of the parallel GL2TriangularSubgroup). Subsequent Schreier generators a*h^-1 then do not stabilize the base vector [0,1], so elements outside the Borel1 subgroup are fed to the GL2Borel1PC isomorphism, causing either an assertion failure (line 687, K`Order eq Xsize*Ssize) or a silently wrong subgroup. Sweeping random 2-generated subgroups mod 8, 12, 15 produced failures in a majority of cases. Also note line 688 repeats the NegOne bug of line 658 (sets L`NegOne := true whenever K`NegOne is assigned, even if false). Correct behavior: return H meet {upper triangular matrices with 1 in bottom right}.

The returned intersection K = H meet Borel gets K`NegOne := true whenever H`NegOne is ASSIGNED, ignoring its value. Per the attribute contract (line 82, NegOne can be true/false/unassigned) this silently corrupts K when H`NegOne is false: -I is diagonal, so -I in K iff -I in H, and the correct propagation is to copy the value. Downstream, GL2ContainsNegativeOne(K) (line 1294) trusts the attribute and returns true for a group that does not contain -I, which poisons any index/genus/cusp logic keyed on -I containment. Natural trigger: GL2Borel1(N) and several other constructors set NegOne := false.

gl1copyattr takes two arguments (Hnew,Hold) but is called with only one, so GL1Project crashes with a wrong-number-of-arguments runtime error whenever H`Level is assigned and M is a multiple of H`Level -- exactly the case the docstring says preserves the level. Any group produced by GL1Ambient, GL1Level or GL1Lift has Level assigned, so this is easy to hit. The parallel GL2Project (line 461) has the correct two-argument call.

When H`Level is already assigned with value 1 and #BaseRing(H) = N > 1, the second return value evaluates ChangeRing(H,Integers(1)), which Magma forbids ('Matrix group over ring of cardinality 1 is forbidden'). It should return gl1N1, mirroring the guard SL2Level has at line 479 and the computed path at line 235. Natural trigger: GL1Ambient(N) sets Level := 1, so GL1Level(GL1Ambient(8)) and GL1Label(GL1Ambient(8)) both crash.

findings.description: In the catch block, the retry recomputes `cnt := ExactQuotient(m*#Fix(pi(g)),n)` and then checks `if Denominator(cnt) ne 1 then print "Retry failed:"...; error e; end if; cnt := Numerator(cnt);`. findings.description: GL2Triangular1Subgroup returns wrong groups and corrupts Order attributes (including the Order attribute of the INPUT group H, which per the file-header warning at lines 90-95 can cause Magma-kernel infinite loops). Two interacting defects: (a) line 682 stores 'T[z] := a*g' where a := T[y]*g already includes the generator, so the Schreier transversal entry becomes T[y]*g^2; the parallel code in GL2TriangularSubgroup (line 652) and GL2Order (line 625) correctly stores 'T[z] := a'. The resulting 'Schreier generators' h := a*T[z]^-1 do not stabilize V=[0,1] and need not lie in the Borel1 group at all. (b) This goes undetected because the pi returned by GL2Borel1PC (line 1824, outside my audit range - flagging for cross-reference) is a func that silently accepts non-Borel1 matrices AND is not even a homomorphism on the Borel1 group {[a,b;0,1]} (pi(h)=Dpi(diag(a,1))*n^b, but the correct iso is n^b*Dpi(diag(a,1)), equivalently exponent b/a): e.g. mod 9, h1=[2,4,0,1], h2=[7,6,0,1] generate a group of order 6 but their pi-images generate a subgroup of P of order 18. So Ssize=#sub<P|pi(h)> is wrong even for inputs contained in Borel1 where defect (a) never triggers. Correct behavior: return H meet {[a,b;0,1]} with correct Order attributes and without mutating H`Order incorrectly. Note both failure modes are hidden whenever K`Order was already assigned and the Smax early-exit fires before corruption matters (e.g. after calling #H first), which is why this survived; the Borel test cases also pass by accident.

findings.description: GL2MinimalConjugate returns non-minimal generator sequences for many subgroups at composite level. The pruning step at lines 3178-3180 selects conjugates by GrpMatElt ordering (Min([k:k in K]) and 'a eq G![1,0,0,1]'), but minimality is defined by Eltseq ordering (as GL2MinimalGenerators' own docstring warns, 'comparing Eltseq(g) to Eltseq(h) ... **differs** from comparing g to h'). When the two orderings disagree (they differ on 2880 ordered pairs already in GL(2,Z/4)), the pruning discards the conjugates containing the Eltseq-minimal elements, and the final Min over the surviving (wrong) conjugates is not the true minimum. Since this function exists solely to compute the tiebreaker of last resort for RSZB labels, wrong output here can produce wrong RSZB labels. At prime levels 2,3,5 and at N=6 brute force found no mismatches; at N=4, 12 of the tested subgroups give wrong (non-minimal) answers.

  MISMATCH N = 4 gens: [[1,0,0,3],[1,2,0,1]]  intrinsic: [[1,0,2,1],[3,0,0,1]]  brute: [[1,0,0,3],[1,2,0,1]]
  MISMATCH N = 4 gens: [[1,3,2,1],[3,2,0,3]]  intrinsic: [[1,2,1,1]]  brute: [[0,1,1,2]]
  ... (12 mismatches total at N=4; 0 at N=2,3,5,6)
In each case the brute answer is lex-smaller (e.g. [1,2,2,1] < [3,0,2,3], [0,1,1,2] < [1,2,1,1]), i.e. the intrinsic's answer is not minimal. Order-mismatch root cause: for G:=GL(2,Integers(4)), #{(g,h): (g lt h) ne (Eltseq(g) lt Eltseq(h))} = 2880. The [0,1,1,0]/[0,1,1,1] shortcut at line 3176 is not at fault (in the failing cases no conjugate contains either matrix). A fixed reimplementation using Eltseq-based pruning matches brute force on all 2465 subgroups tested across N in {2,3,4,5,6,8} (0 mismatches).

findings.description: The three returned values are mutually inconsistent, and the third return value (claimed isomorphism B1 -> P) is not even a homomorphism. The R-version docstring (line 1809) says the group has '1 in the bottom right (not the top left!)', and the polycyclic presentation (rels3 exponent pi(-gg[i]) at line 1817), the auxiliary diagonal group D = <[pi(g),0,0,1]> (line 1822), and the map func (line 1824) are all written for the bottom-right-1 convention {[a,x;0,1]}. But G is generated by [[1,0,0,pi(g)]] (line 1818), i.e. 1 in the UPPER left. On G's own elements the map collapses the diagonal part (it reads g[1][1], which is always 1), so f(diag(1,2)) = Id(P); and even on bottom-right-1 matrices it is not multiplicative because the unipotent exponent must be g[1][2]/g[1][1], not g[1][2] (compare GL2BorelPC line 1798, which divides). Correct behavior: G := {[a,x;0,1]} and f(g) = Dpi(D![g[1][1],0,0,1])*n^(g[1][2]/g[1][1]); I implemented this candidate fix locally and verified it is an injective homomorphism with #G eq #P for N = 5,8,9,12. Also the N-version docstring (line 1828) says 'a 1 in the upper left', contradicting the R-version; with the fix below it should say bottom right. Consequence: GL2Triangular1Subgroup (line 662, the only caller, itself outside my range) returns wrong groups and crashes (see separate finding).

findings.description: GL2RationalCuspCount(H, q) is wrong (prime level) or crashes (odd prime-power level) when q = 1 mod N and GL2DeterminantIndex(H) > 1. The early return at line 1482 handles q = 1 mod N only when the determinant index is 1; otherwise d := [q,0,0,1] is the identity matrix and (a) for prime N line 1485 returns the permutation character of the identity, which counts fixed COSETS ([GL2:H]) instead of fixed T-orbits (= GL2CuspCount(H)); (b) for odd prime-power N line 1487 calls IsPrimePower(Order(d)) = IsPrimePower(1), a runtime error. Correct value when q = 1 mod N: Frobenius acts trivially, so every cusp is Fq-rational and the answer is GL2CuspCount(H); this matches the slow path (which counts T-orbits of H\\GL2 fixed by pi(d)) and matches GL2RationalCuspCounts, which already sets c[1] := GL2CuspCount(H) unconditionally. The composite-N branch (line 1494) is unaffected (its Burnside average over d*T^n correctly reduces to the orbit count).

GL2ArithK1(1,2) sets the built-in Order attribute to 4 on a group of order 2 (the formula (N div M)*2*EulerPhi(N) double-counts at N=2 because -I = I, so the generator [-1,0,0,-1] is the identity), and consequently Index is set to 6 div 4 = 1 while the true index is 3. Magma trusts the Order attribute, so #H itself reports 4 and GL2Index returns 1 - the group object is corrupted. The sibling constructors all special-case #R eq 2 (GL2SplitCartanK1 line 1654, GL2BorelK1 line 1902, GL2BorelK12 line 1917); GL2ArithK1 misses it. Only M=1, N=2 is affected (M=N=2 returns GL2SplitCartanK1(2), which is handled).

The 'if IsOdd(N) and IsPrime(N)' block (lines 1751-1755) is dead code with wrong content: it builds NC from GL2SplitCartan(N) (a copy-paste from GL2SplitCartanNormalizer - for the nonsplit normalizer it should start from a nonsplit Cartan) and then never returns it, falling through to the generic GL2CartanNormalizer(D,N) path. Worse, the added generator [1,0,0,-1] is diagonal, hence already inside the split Cartan, so NC = GL2SplitCartan(N) - if someone 'fixed' the missing return, the function would silently return the split Cartan. Current returned values are correct (verified equal to the true normalizer of the nonsplit Cartan for p = 5,7,13); the only present-day cost is a wasted GL2SplitCartan construction per prime-level call, plus the NC`Index := C`Index div 2 line which mislabels attributes on a discarded object.

findings.description: Several constructors hard-code NegOne := false, which is wrong at N=2 where -I = I lies in every subgroup: GL2SplitCartan1 (line 1643), GL2Arith1 (line 1684), GL2Borel1 (line 1876), and GL2BorelK1(2) (line 1902, which returns GL2Borel1(R)). Since GL2ContainsNegativeOne (line 1297) returns the cached attribute, it reports false for groups that contain -I; downstream, GL2QAdmissible(H:MustContainNegativeOne:=true) would wrongly reject such level-2 groups. Note GL2SplitCartanK1 explicitly special-cases #R eq 2 with NegOne := true for essentially the same group, showing intended semantics; GL2Borel12/GL2BorelK12 at #R=2 go through GL2FromGenerators without setting NegOne and behave correctly.

findings.description: For N=2 and D odd with 2 inert (D = 5 mod 8, e.g. D=-3), the Cartan normalizer is all of GL(2,Z/2) (order 6), whose level as an open subgroup is 1, but the code unconditionally sets CN`Level := N = 2. GL2Level then returns the cached 2, inconsistent with GL2Index = 1 and with the true level 1. (This is exactly why GL2NonsplitCartanNormalizer special-cases N le 2; direct calls to GL2CartanNormalizer are still exposed.) All other (D,N) are fine: for N>2 the normalizer cannot contain the full reduction kernel, and for N=2 with D even or D split the group is proper.

findings.description: GL2SturmBound(1) raises 'Runtime error in &*: Illegal null sequence' because Factorization(1) yields an empty sequence with no universe. For every N >= 2 the value was verified to equal psi(N^2)*phi(N)/6 (index of Gamma_1(N) meet Gamma_0(N^2) in SL2(Z) times k/12 with k=2), consistent with the docstring; the N=1 value should be 0 (S_2(SL2(Z)) = 0).

For all N in [2..12] and D in {-3,-4,-7,-8,-11,-12,-15,-16,-19,-20,-27,-28,-75} the formula was verified against a direct count of units in O/NO (and against #UnitGroup(O_K/N O_K) for fundamental D). findings.description: SL2BorelPC(1) uses gl2N1 instead of sl2N1: 'if N eq 1 then B := gl2N1; ...' - the returned group is not marked with the SL attribute, unlike every other SL2 constructor (SL2Borel(1) returns sl2N1). findings.description: The Borel-family constructors with R::Rng signatures (GL2Borel line 1767, SL2Borel 1834, GL2Borel1 1872, GL2Borel12 1885, GL2BorelK1 1900, GL2BorelK12 1914) set the BUILT-IN Order/Index/Level attributes using formulas valid only for R = Z/N (GL2BorelSize(#R) etc.). For any other finite commutative ring the signature accepts, e.g. GF(4), the group object is corrupted: Magma trusts the asserted Order, so #GL2Borel(GF(4)) reports 16 although the group has 36 elements. The RngIntRes-only constructors (GL2SplitCartan etc.) are properly guarded; these six are not.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the six signatures from (R::Rng) to (R::RngIntRes), or add at the top of each: 'require Type(R) eq RngIntRes: "R must be Z/NZ for some N > 1";' (GL2BorelPC/GL2Borel1PC/SL2BorelPC have the same exposure via their R::Rng signatures and could get the same guard).

findings.description: Docstring (both R and N versions, lines 1714 and 1721) claims the algebraic split Cartan normalizer 'is equal to the normalizer in GL(2,Z/NZ) only when N is a prime power'. This is false for powers of 2: at N=4 the intrinsic returns order 8 but the actual normalizer of the split Cartan in GL(2,Z/4) has order 32; at N=8, 32 vs 128 (and at N=2, 2 vs 6). Equality was verified to hold at N = 5,7,9,13,25. Should say 'odd prime power'. Relatedly, GL2SplitCartanFullNormalizer's docstring (line 1726) 'properly contains GL2SplitCartanNormalizer when #R is not prime' is wrong in both directions (equal at the non-prime values 9 and 25; proper at the primes-power... at 4 and 8 and at the prime 2) and references '#R' though the parameter is N; and GL2NonsplitCartanFullNormalizer (line 1762) says 'properly contains GL2NonsplitCartanNormalizer when N is not prime' although they were verified EQUAL at the non-primes 4, 8 and 9 (proper containment starts at non-prime-powers, verified at 12, 15).
findings.proposed_fix:
Line 1714 and 1721: '...only when N is a prime power' -> '...only when N is an odd prime power'.
Line 1726: 'properly contains GL2SplitCartanNormalizer when #R is not prime' -> 'properly contains GL2SplitCartanNormalizer when N is not an odd prime power'.
Line 1762: 'properly contains GL2NonsplitCartanNormalizer when N is not prime' -> 'properly contains GL2NonsplitCartanNormalizer when N is not a prime power'.

findings.description: The branch 'elif p mod 8 eq 1 then' is unreachable: it is only tested when a ne 1, but a := (p mod 8 in [1,7]) select 1 else 2, so a ne 1 implies p mod 8 in {3,5}. All p = 1 mod 8 take the first branch. (Possibly a leftover case split from Flannery-O'Brien Thm 5.8.) Also the variable t assigned at line 1998 is never used.
